rows.subtopic: A promotion and the ego that follows
rows.description: Former teammates feel dropped and second-guess whether to speak up. They stop offering ideas, which hides problems from the lead and makes the team quieter, not stronger.

rows.subtopic: A promotion and the ego that follows
rows.description: Critical remarks are brushed off as jealousy or lack of vision. The ego protects a new identity by treating any challenge as a threat, and the leader stops learning.
graph_context: previous stage: Distance from former peers

rows.subtopic: A promotion and the ego that follows
rows.description: A poor call made without consulting others costs the team a delay. Blame is first pushed onto the team, and the leader feels shaken as the halo cracks.
graph_context: next stage: Humbling and honest reflection

rows.subtopic: A promotion and the ego that follows
rows.description: The lead owns the error openly, thanks those who warned them and asks for candid feedback. Acknowledging fault in public tends to raise respect rather than lower it.

rows.subtopic: A promotion and the ego that follows
rows.description: The leader reframes the role as clearing obstacles and growing others, credits the team and stays close to former peers. Authority earned by service outlasts authority claimed by position.
graph_context: previous stage: Humbling and honest reflection

rows.subtopic: A promotion and the ego that follows
rows.description: A mentor sees a newly promoted friend start to talk in the first person about every team win. A private, kind remark that the team now notices the credit-taking can save a career.
graph_context: previous stage: The news and the glow
next stage: Distance from former peers

rows.subtopic: Drawn into a high-control group or online extremism
rows.description: A lonely teenager, unsettled by exams or family strain, meets a warm group or online community that offers attention, meaning and friends. Recruitment works by meeting real needs first, before any demands appear.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtopic: Drawn into a high-control group or online extremism
rows.description: The newcomer is praised, included in chats and given a role. Belonging feels like being finally understood, and the intensity of the welcome makes leaving later feel like a loss.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtopic: Drawn into a high-control group or online extremism
rows.description: The group starts to describe outsiders, parents and old friends as blind, corrupt or hostile. The person begins to see the world in two camps, and doubts are read as weakness or influence of outsiders.
graph_context: next stage: Rising demands and isolation
this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26

rows.subtopic: Drawn into a high-control group or online extremism
rows.description: Time, money and secrecy are increasingly required, and contact with family or dissenting friends falls. Each step is small enough to accept, and past sacrifice makes the next feel necessary.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26
